stores.name: Almond River Records
stores.description: Curated second-hand shop in west Edinburgh offering ultrasonic record cleaning and fair cash/trade on collections.
stores.bio: Founded by passionate crate diggers, Almond River Records is West Edinburgh's premier haven for quality second-hand vinyl, CDs, and audio gear. Specialising in meticulously graded 60s/70s classic rock, prog, indie, and jazz, every pre-loved record is inspected with care, and ultrasonic deep-cleaning is available in-store to bring vintage grooves back to life. A friendly, knowledgeable neighbourhood hub that actively buys collections with fair cash or trade appraisals.

stores.name: Veneno Music Store
stores.description: Welcoming Fife independent with super honest condition grading across pre-loved and new vinyl.
stores.bio: Located in historic Dunfermline just across the Queensferry Crossing, Veneno Music Store has quickly earned a glowing reputation for its curated crates of heavy rock, metal, 90s alternative, and punk alongside fresh indie pressings. The store champions physical formats with transparent condition grading, dedicated listening decks where you can audition before you buy, and an active trade-in counter welcoming wax collectors from across Fife and the Lothians.

stores.name: The Music Box
stores.description: Independent Dunfermline spot strong on UK indie rarities, limited box sets, and pre-owned crates.
stores.bio: A relatively new outlet opening juat over a year ago servicing the Dunfermline and broader area music community, The Music Box is an old-school treasure trove packed to the rafters with rock, folk, blues, and pop vinyl across 12-inch LPs and 7-inch singles. Renowned for its bargain discovery crates and deep CD archives, it's the definition of a traditional digger's spot where taking your time flipping through the stacks is always rewarded with forgotten classics at honest prices.

stores.name: VoxBox Music
stores.description: Famous for pristine front-shop stock and the legendary £1-£3 bargain basement room out back.

reviews.comment: Front racks are immaculately clean, and the £2 backroom always yields a weird library record or 12-inch for sampling.

stores.bio: Tucked away on cobbled St Stephen Street in Stockbridge, VoxBox Music is one of Scotland's most beloved vinyl sanctuaries. Spread across two atmospheric rooms of vintage records, VoxBox specialises in original UK pressings of classic rock, blues, jazz, and Scottish indie, accompanied by bargain £1.50 crates in the back room. The staff are seasoned musicians and collectors who pride themselves on strictly honest visual and audio grading without inflated collector hype.

stores.name: Oxfam Music Stockbridge
stores.description: Dedicated music charity shop receiving some of Edinburgh's best donated vinyl collections.
stores.bio: Celebrated as one of the UK's flagship charity music shops, Oxfam Music on Raeburn Place is a legendary goldmine for Edinburgh vinyl hunters. Run by devoted music-enthusiast volunteers who carefully curate every incoming estate and donation, its shelves constantly rotate with rare classical, folk, jazz, classic rock, and quirky 7-inch obscurities, all fairly priced with proceeds supporting global humanitarian causes.

stores.name: Low Port Music
stores.description: Linlithgow's local independent record shop. Great for indie exclusives, Ninja Tune/4AD/Soul Jazz releases, and RSD drops.
stores.bio: Just steps from historic Linlithgow Palace and the canal basin, Low Port Music is a vibrant West Lothian institution. Combining a passion for indie, rock, Scottish folk, and Americana vinyl with musical instruments, turntable accessories, and guitar strings, owner Chris has created a warm, community-first space where locals and visiting diggers can chat gear, swap music recommendations, and unearth pristine vintage wax.

stores.name: Greenhouse Records
stores.description: Specialist shop dealing in underground club 12-inches, electronic, dub, and global experimental sounds.
stores.bio: Perched in leafy Bruntsfield, Greenhouse Records is a chic, daylight-filled sanctuary for audiophiles and curious selectors. With an impeccably curated roster spanning ambient, jazz, electronic, soul, and left-field indie, Greenhouse champions small independent labels, local Edinburgh releases, and pristine Japanese pressings, paired with a welcoming vibe and listening stations to lose yourself in.

stores.name: Umbrella Vinyl
stores.description: Play-graded specialist second-hand shop covering global sounds, deep jazz, funk, dub, and library records.

reviews.comment: Every used record is play-graded and ultrasonic cleaned. You can trust their VG+ sticker without hesitation.

stores.bio: Situated on Valleyfield Street in Tollcross, Umbrella Vinyl is run by two dedicated diggers who hand-pick their stock across the globe. Famous for an eclectic, genre-spanning selection that dives deep into 70s Japanese funk, city pop, reggae, Afrobeat, psych, and post-punk, Umbrella treats vinyl digging as an art form. Every record is clean, sleeved, accurately graded, and ready for home or club listening.

stores.name: Assai Records
stores.description: Spacious new-release powerhouse known for numbered Japanese-style Obi editions and hardware/sleeves.
stores.bio: Overlooking Grindlay Street beneath Edinburgh Castle, Assai Records Edinburgh is a flagship indie retailer known for its premier stock of brand-new vinyl releases, exclusive Assai limited-edition obi-strip pressings, and high-end audio turntables. Hosting intimate in-store acoustic gigs and signing sessions from internationally touring artists, Assai is a cornerstone of the Scottish modern music scene.

stores.name: Backtracks Music
stores.description: Old-school floor-to-ceiling crate digger's staple with thousands of used LPs and 45s.
stores.bio: Standing strong on Brougham Street since 1989, Backtracks is Edinburgh's classic collector's depot. Packed with thousands of retro vinyl records, cassette tapes, CDs, vintage hi-fi separates, and music memorabilia, it's a paradise for diggers who love the thrill of the hunt. Whether you're searching for original 70s rock LPs, rare 80s 12-inch dance mixes, or replacement turntable needles, Backtracks has it in the bins.

stores.name: Thorne Records
stores.description: Dog-friendly neighbourhood shop with super clean rack spacing and thoughtfully curated new pressings.
stores.bio: Founded by veteran record store manager Mark Thorne, this bright, welcoming South Edinburgh boutique on Bruntsfield Place offers an expertly chosen balance of brand-new indie releases, classic reissues, and curated second-hand gems. Known for its warm hospitality, knowledgeable personal recommendations, and spotless organization, Thorne Records makes browsing feel effortless and joyful for collectors of every generation.

stores.name: Underground Solu'shn
stores.description: Edinburgh's institution for DJs and beatmakers: dance 12s, hip-hop, jazz reissues, Ortofon carts, and Technics accessories.

reviews.comment: Still the undisputed king for dance 12s, hip-hop beats, and grabbing replacement styli in town.

stores.bio: An undisputed cultural landmark on Cockburn Street since 1995, Underground Solu'shn is the heartbeat of Edinburgh's electronic, club, and DJ culture. Stocking deep crates of house, techno, drum & bass, hip-hop, funk, soul, and jazz alongside professional DJ hardware, synthesizers, and vinyl care supplies, 'US' is the definitive meeting ground for local DJs, visiting selectors, and sound enthusiasts.

stores.name: Slow Progress Records & Coffee
stores.description: Independent record shop and specialty coffee bar tucked just off the Royal Mile.
stores.bio: Combining the finest specialty plant-based coffee, bakery treats, and an expertly curated vinyl selection on Blackfriars Street, Slow Progress is a cosy haven just off the Royal Mile. Specialising in emo, punk, hardcore, post-rock, and alternative indie labels, you can enjoy a flat white while browsing limited-run vinyl or auditioning new underground bands on their customer turntables.

stores.name: Vinyl Villains
stores.description: At the top of Leith Walk since 1982. Deep second-hand racks and unpretentious staff knowledge.
stores.bio: Holding court at the top of Leith Walk on Elm Row since 1983, Vinyl Villains is Edinburgh's oldest surviving independent second-hand record shop. Packed floor-to-ceiling with vintage rock, punk, new wave, prog, metal, and reggae vinyl, its seasoned crates have provided generations of crate diggers with authentic first pressings, rare bootlegs, and bargain gems at honest, realistic prices.

stores.name: Lounge 33
stores.description: Vinyl listening space and specialty coffee lounge built around jazz, soul, funk, and hip-hop records.

reviews.best_pull: Thievery Corporation - The Richest Man in Babylon
reviews.comment: Grab a flat white from Mr Eion beans, sit down with a stack of jazz and trip-hop records, and lose an afternoon.

stores.bio: An intimate, relaxed record den located on middle Leith Walk, Lounge 33 combines a passion for vintage vinyl with comfortable, music-first vibes. Featuring a hand-picked collection of soul, funk, disco, jazz, 90s hip-hop, and classic rock, it's designed as a laid-back retreat where music fans can take their time thumbing through carefully graded sleeves and discovering new grooves.

stores.name: Good Vibes Neighbourhood Store
stores.description: Curated selection of specialist labels, spiritual jazz, ambient, and psyche in the heart of Leith.
stores.bio: Situated down on Constitution Street in historic Leith, Good Vibes Neighbourhood Store is a community-minded creative hub. Stocking a vibrant selection of new and pre-loved vinyl—with a keen focus on soul, afro-funk, indie, electronic, and Scottish grassroots releases—alongside curated books, local art, and artisan provisions, it brings genuine warmth and good tunes to the port district.

stores.name: Avalanche Records
stores.description: Long-running champion of Scottish independent bands alongside vintage vinyl crates.
stores.bio: Originally established in 1984 and now housed within the Waverley Market directly above Edinburgh Waverley Station, Avalanche Records is an iconic Scottish music brand. Renowned historically for supporting Scottish indie royalty including Belle & Sebastian, Mogwai, and Frightened Rabbit, Avalanche pairs Scottish indie and alternative vinyl with vintage rock art prints, band t-shirts, and cultural memorabilia.

stores.name: Silver Machine Records
stores.description: Vintage and rare vinyl specialist on Falkirk High Street with deep crates of classic rock and metal.
stores.bio: Located inside The Avenue on Falkirk's High Street, Silver Machine Records is Central Scotland's champion for classic and rare vinyl. Named with a nod to Hawkwind, the shop is a treasure chest of vintage 60s/70s/80s rock, heavy metal, prog, psych, and folk. Known for fair pricing, friendly rock banter, and an ever-rotating inventory of clean pre-loved vinyl, it's an essential stop on any Forth Valley crate-digging expedition.

stores.name: Europa Music
stores.description: One of Scotland's largest independent record shops, trading since 1992 with massive collections across all genres.
stores.bio: Established in 1992 on Friars Street in Stirling, Europa Music is one of Scotland's largest and most legendary independent music stores. Housed in a sprawling traditional shopfront just 22 miles from South Queensferry, it boasts tens of thousands of new and second-hand vinyl records spanning rock, folk, blues, jazz, punk, reggae, and classical, plus a massive CD and cassette department. A true Scottish crate-digging cathedral.

stores.name: D&J Records
stores.description: Beloved West Lothian vinyl and CD shop packed with pre-owned classics, plus professional in-store record flattening.
stores.bio: Located on George Street in the heart of Bathgate, D&J Records is a cherished West Lothian hub for collectors and everyday music fans. Offering a warm, welcoming community feel with an extensive stock of pre-owned 12" vinyl, 7" singles, CDs, and audio gear across rock, pop, soul, country, and Scottish traditional music, D&J also provides a specialist vinyl flattening service to rescue warped records—making it an essential local crate-digging stop.

stores.name: JPMJ Vinyl @ Flemings Antique Centre
stores.description: Extensive vintage vinyl selection inside Flemings Antique Centre, with on-site Majestic Tea Room just 3 miles across the Forth.
stores.bio: Located just across the Queensferry Crossing in Inverkeithing, JPMJ Vinyl is a hidden crate-digging treasure housed within the sprawling Fleming's Furniture & Antique Centre. Boasting a deep and ever-rotating selection of vintage wax, the crates cover every golden era—from 50s rock 'n' roll and 70s prog to heavy metal, Northern soul, jazz, and classic 80s/90s pop. With the charming on-site Majestic Tea Room serving tea, coffee, and home baking, it makes for a fantastic and relaxed afternoon dig just 3 miles from South Queensferry.

stores.name: KCC Vinyl
stores.description: Friendly Fife independent record store in the Kingdom Centre specialising in pre-owned vinyl, CDs, and guitars.
stores.bio: Located inside the Kingdom Shopping Centre on Unicorn Way in Glenrothes, KCC Vinyl is a friendly local haven for Fife music lovers and crate diggers. Specialising in carefully curated pre-owned 12" vinyl LPs, 7" singles, CDs, vintage guitars, and music memorabilia, KCC brings a warm, community record shop vibe to central Fife with plenty of bargain discovery crates, classic rock, indie, metal, and pop wax.

stores.name: Backbeat Records
stores.description: Legendary Southside institution since 1981 holding over 65,000 vintage records and CDs stacked high to the ceiling.
stores.bio: A Southside Edinburgh fixture since 1981, Backbeat Records on East Crosscauseway is run by legendary owner Dougie McShane. An astonishing treasure labyrinth holding more than 65,000 vintage second-hand records and CDs across a warren of rooms, stock is literally stacked several records deep and reaching up to the ceiling. Packed with rare prog, psychedelia, jazz, reggae, punk, 60s rock, and film soundtracks, it is the definition of an authentic old-school crate digger's temple. Bring a want list—Dougie knows every corner of the stacks.
